## Summary

Build the first portfolio homepage from the approved Portfolio V2 prototype, using the current AI engineering and full-stack positioning.

```text
src/
├── app/          homepage, shared layout and not-found route
├── components/   navigation, themes and project overview dialogs
├── content/      reviewed homepage summaries
└── styles/       tokens and responsive layouts
```

Includes strict React/TypeScript/Vite, Tailwind v4, self-hosted fonts, prerendered homepage/404 HTML, quality CI and engineering documentation. Full content routes and publishing automation remain deferred. The prototype stays local in ignored `docs/engineering/` and is absent from the branch.

## Evidence

- **Before:** empty application foundation; approved HTML prototype available locally.
  **After:** `pnpm check` passed (formatting, Oxlint, strict types, 6 component/unit tests); `pnpm build` passed; `pnpm test:e2e` passed all 12 Chromium desktop/mobile tests.
- Light/dark screenshots were compared with the prototype. Tested axe states reported no violations; overflow checks passed at 320, 390, 768, 1440 and 1920px.
- After moving the prototype and updating ignore rules/documentation, `pnpm format:check` passed. Git's tracked file list contains neither `reference/` nor `docs/engineering/`.
- Project summaries retain documented status and privacy boundaries. No source-project tests or remote CI results are claimed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A new static application with no backend, migrations or deployment performed. Production deployment still requires explicit approval.

**Blast Radius:** portfolio

Merging adds the application and quality workflow to the new, owner-approved public repository. The archived reference repository and existing live site remain unchanged.

## Summary

Moves production release control into a separate visible GitHub workflow while retaining PR previews.

```text
main push → Quality succeeds → verify current tested SHA + environment rules
→ required production approval → build exact SHA → stage without domains
→ static-content/HTTP 404 smoke checks → recheck main → promote → public smoke
```

Disables only Vercel automatic main deployments, adds the GitHub production environment URL/job summary and README status badge, and records architecture/setup/recovery guidance. Uses pinned actions/CLI and protected environment credentials; no PR artifacts are used. About work was delivered separately in merged PR #4; this branch is based on its merge commit.

**Do not merge until environment/credential setup is complete.** Read-only inspection found no GitHub environments. Draft remains open for setup and owner review; no environment, secret, live Vercel setting or production deployment was changed by this task.

## Evidence

- **Before:** Vercel Git integration deployed main independently of Quality; Quality itself had no deployment step.
  **After:** the proposed Production workflow runs only for successful main push Quality completions, requires enforced human review/main-only environment rules and rejects PR, failed, foreign and stale runs. It stages the tested production build before assigning domains.
- `pnpm --config.verifyDepsBeforeRun=false check`: passed formatting, lint, strict types, 8 component/unit tests and 12 guard/smoke tests.
- `pnpm --config.verifyDepsBeforeRun=false build`: passed; four valid static pages and the 404 generated on the updated main base.
- `actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/production.yml` with actionlint 1.7.12: passed. Shellcheck was unavailable; its integration was disabled.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Pinned Vercel 65.16.0 package code confirms environment-token authentication.
- The pnpm flag avoids reinstalling unchanged dependencies through this temporary worktree's shared node_modules symlink. No dependency inputs changed.
- Guard tests cover failed/PR/foreign/wrong-workflow runs, stale SHA, missing reviewer and broad branch policies. Smoke tests cover generated-page discovery, incomplete HTML, wrong content, SPA fallback 200 and cross-origin redirect rejection.
- No live deployment/promotion or real approval gate was exercised. The first end-to-end run needs explicit owner approval after setup.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Workflow/config can be reverted; existing production remains live while waiting for approval. Failed post-promotion smoke checks report failure and require an explicit recovery decision; no automatic rollback.

**Blast Radius:** production

Merging disables automatic main releases. Configure GitHub `production` with required reviewers and exactly one selected branch rule `main`, plus environment secrets `VERCEL_TOKEN` and `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET`, before merging. Otherwise the guard refuses deployment and automatic main release is already disabled. See `docs/operations/production-deployment.md` for cutover and recovery. No merge/deployment is authorized by opening this PR.

## Summary

The portfolio still describes Release Log’s workflow as undeployed. Expand the homepage/index summary and case study around packaged CLI availability, the reviewed release cycle, deterministic replay, documented self-use and remaining AI/validation boundaries. Narrative evidence is pinned to public README commit `033903ca288b623d0014e5e0e23de354b5668ea8`, reviewed 2026-11-16; no source-project tests or private sandbox material were collected.

```text
Open case study
  → render reviewed content and current upstream usage link
  → query public GitHub version refs after hydration
  → show highest stable vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag
  → retain ordinary links on failure, timeout or disabled JavaScript
```

Future stable tags, including v0.3.0 once tagged, appear on later visits without a website commit or deployment. Prereleases are excluded. A source tag does not assert that a matching container has published; runnable image/digest instructions stay upstream. README and ADR 0003 document the behavior.

## Evidence

- **Before:** page says the reusable workflow is not deployed, calls the CLI locally packable, and leaves provider integration undecided.
  **After:** reviewed copy covers the published Linux/amd64 container, active self-use, proposal refresh → human merge → exact tag, and implemented optional text generation while keeping AI-written notes planned.
- `pnpm check` passed: formatting, lint, strict TypeScript, 21 component/unit tests and 12 deployment tests.
- `pnpm build` passed; inspected generated HTML for expanded copy, current metadata, pinned provenance and no-JavaScript usage/tag links. No live version is baked into the static document.
- `pnpm test:e2e` passed: 36 desktop/mobile Chromium tests, including simulated v0.3.0 resolution, prerelease exclusion, GitHub 403 fallback, no-JavaScript content, navigation, axe, themes, reduced motion and overflow at 320–1920px. Browser suite required permission to start the local preview outside the sandbox.
- Inspected case-study screenshots in light/dark desktop/mobile layouts. `git diff --check` passed.
- No hosted HTTP-status check or production deployment was performed. Live GitHub refs were read separately; automated tests mock the API for repeatability.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores the prior static copy and removes the optional version lookup. No dependency, workflow, hosting or production configuration changes.

**Blast Radius:** portfolio

The case study makes one credential-free, referrer-free browser request to GitHub on mount, with a five-second timeout. GitHub receives ordinary visitor network metadata; rate limits or network failures keep fallback links. The curated narrative still requires human review for capability changes. This PR does not authorize merge or production deployment.

## Summary

Production run [43963778042](https://github.com/lhajoosten/lucjoosten.nl/actions/runs/43963778042) successfully built, staged and smoke-tested commit `6085708a72a40f7f4b5902bde63fd264dce454e8`, then `vercel promote` failed with `User not found. (404)`. The staged deployment is READY production with no aliases. The pinned CLI's promotion path performs a personal-user context lookup; a synthetic 404 reproduces the symptom even with explicit team scope. Earlier team build/deploy operations succeeded with the same workflow credentials.

Replace only promotion with the documented [team-scoped REST API](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/projects/point-production-traffic-to-a-given-deployment), retaining all Quality/current-main/reviewer/smoke gates.

```text
final GitHub guard
  → validate fixed project/team ownership
  → validate staged URL + READY production target + tested SHA
  → submit one promotion request with teamId
  → await that exact deployment's successful alias request
  → existing public production smoke checks
```

No credential rotation or broader personal-account permissions are required by this implementation. No preview rebuild, automatic POST retry, rollback, DNS change or live promotion is included. Operations guidance records the observed environment and promotion failures; ADR 0002 records the narrower promotion implementation.

## Evidence

- **Before:** CLI context-resolution functions extracted from published `@vercel/cli-support@65.16.0` reproduce `User not found. (404)` for a synthetic user lookup failure, with and without explicit team scope. This is a local reproduction of the CLI path; the live run did not expose an HTTP trace proving the exact failing request.
  **After:** promotion fixtures provide team project/deployment access while personal-user access returns 404; the helper succeeds without requesting `/v2/user`.
- `pnpm check` passed: formatting, lint, strict TypeScript, 21 component/unit tests, 12 existing guard/smoke tests and 9 new promotion tests. Fixtures cover pending/success/failure, wrong URL/project/team/commit/target, and rejected/uncertain POSTs without retries.
- `pnpm build` passed; no application UI changes.
- `/tmp/actionlint-bin/actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/production.yml` passed. Shellcheck integration disabled because shellcheck is unavailable.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- No live promotion with the changed helper has been executed. Production verification remains pending review, merge and the protected workflow run.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores the CLI promotion step. Credentials remain in protected environment variables; API requests refuse redirects and do not print response bodies.

**Blast Radius:** deployment

The production workflow now uses a Node REST helper for promotion and waits up to about three minutes for confirmed alias success. A timeout/uncertain POST can mean the server accepted the request; inspect state before any manual retry. Failed identity checks stop before promotion. The existing required approval, exact-main checks, staged smoke checks and post-promotion public checks remain enforced. No merge or production deployment is authorized by this PR.

## Summary

Production run [43967677181](https://github.com/lhajoosten/lucjoosten.nl/actions/runs/43967677181) promoted commit `53e394b079060a9a64b08fbf083f1a20769a0aef` successfully but timed out while confirming project job-status fields. Read-only Vercel inspection verified that `lucjoosten.nl` maps to the exact staged deployment `dpl_A8oieHV2cXWXJZC7E51bxJ4cfMG3` and that its production aliases completed. The existing confirmation logic did not recognize that state.

```diff
 promotion accepted
-  require matching project job-status fields to report succeeded
+  require lucjoosten.nl to map to the verified deployment in the expected project
 public production smoke checks
```

Read the documented [alias API](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/aliases/get-an-alias) using the existing team scope. Poll through a missing or old mapping; reject unexpected project/domain/redirect identities and authorization failures. Retain explicit failed-job detection for the same deployment, all pre-promotion identity checks and single-submit/no-automatic-retry behavior. Update operations guidance and ADR 0002.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `node scripts/deployment/promote.test.mjs` failed the new completed-domain/missing-job-fields regression with the exact reported `Promotion completion was not confirmed; inspect Vercel before retrying.` error (9 other tests passed).
  **After:** all 13 promotion tests pass, including that regression, delayed mapping, unrelated older job, wrong deployment/project, redirected domain, alias 404/403 and uncertain POST behavior.
- `pnpm check` passed: formatting, lint, strict TypeScript, 21 component/unit tests, 12 guard/smoke tests and 13 promotion tests.
- `pnpm build`, `git diff --check` and the final targeted format check passed. No workflow YAML or application UI changes.
- Read-only `node scripts/deployment/smoke.mjs https://lucjoosten.nl` passed against the already live deployment: `/`, `/about`, `/projects` and `/projects/release-log` returned HTTP 200 with expected initial headings/metadata; an unknown route returned the custom noindex HTTP 404.
- No promotion was repeated, no failed run was retried and no deployment was created during this recovery. The failed run remains failed; its skipped public checks were performed separately. A subsequent approved workflow run still needs to exercise the corrected helper live.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores the previous confirmation strategy; it does not roll back the already live site.

**Blast Radius:** deployment

Confirmation now depends on read access to the canonical production alias. Authorization errors remain failures; only a 404 is treated as a not-yet-visible mapping. A succeeded project job alone cannot confirm the wrong serving deployment. Existing approval, current-main guards, staged/public smoke checks and no-retry promotion boundaries remain unchanged. No merge or production mutation is requested by this PR.
